dedupe_keys.name: tarbela dam pakistan reservoir sedimentation case study with the ressass delta model hr wallingford

description: This paper by HR Wallingford presents Tarbela reservoir on the Indus River, built between 1968 and 1974 for irrigation supply, power and flood control, as a case study of reservoir sedimentation. It reports that sediment has cut the initial capacity of 11,600 million cubic metres by 30 percent and that the advance of the delta foreset slope raises the risk of blocking the low level outlets that supply the irrigation system and power station. The authors use historical survey data on the deposits to validate the numerical model RESSASS, which predicts delta advance accurately, and discuss the influence of upstream reservoirs that could reduce the sediment reaching Tarbela and the sediment passing through turbines. Coverage: one reservoir over four decades. Access: a free eprint; the licence is CC BY. Caveats: only the abstract was read, and the model code is not offered. It supports reservoir capacity loss and sediment management modelling, and relates to the GloRS global reservoir sedimentation data in the catalogue.
